  "problem": "P2P and networking code inconsistently uses durations, raw int64_t timestamps, and deprecated GetTime() alongside NodeClock time points to represent absolute times.     "Commit fafd1e3312: \"Changing the time points to be more precise may change the sorting of the worst peers when they all announced a block in the same second. In this case it should be fine and preferable, to use the more accurate sorting from the exact block announce time for the worst peers, than to fall back to peer with the highest id.\""

result.summary: Replaces deprecated GetTime() calls and duration types with strongly typed NodeClock::time_point and NodeSeconds across networking and P2P modules. The changes span net_processing, txrequest, txdownloadman, and node eviction tracking, while standardizing sentinel values on NodeClock::epoch, time_point::min(), and time_point::max().
result.problem: P2P and networking code inconsistently uses durations, raw int64_t timestamps, and deprecated GetTime() alongside NodeClock time points to represent absolute times. This inconsistency causes type confusion and leads to second-level truncation in peer tracking fields, causing eviction sorting logic to fall back to arbitrary peer IDs during same-second ties.
evidence: PR description: "It is a bit confusing to have some code use the deprecated GetTime, which returns a duration and not a time point, and other code to use NodeClock time points."
Commit fab33fdd92: "With the precision increase from seconds to nanoseconds, SelectNodeToEvict will be more precise picking the protected peers with CompareNodeBlockTime and CompareNodeTXTime."

Commit fafd1e3312: "Changing the time points to be more precise may change the sorting of the worst peers when they all announced a block in the same second. In this case it should be fine and preferable, to use the more accurate sorting from the exact block announce time for the worst peers, than to fall back to peer with the highest id."
result.scope_notes: Modifies time parameter types in public and internal interfaces across several P2P subsystems (txrequest, txdownloadman, eviction, net_processing), requiring coordinated updates across unit tests and fuzz harnesses.
result.card: Replaces deprecated GetTime calls and duration types with NodeClock::time_point and NodeSeconds across P2P subsystems, including net_processing, txrequest, txdownloadman, and peer eviction logic. Inconsistent use of raw integer durations creates type confusion and truncates event timestamps to whole seconds. The author notes that higher timestamp precision improves peer eviction decisions in SelectNodeToEvict and EvictExtraOutboundPeers by sorting based on actual event order rather than falling back to peer IDs during ties. This is primarily an internal refactoring with minor peer sorting precision improvements.
